first.rationale: Verify the directly relevant onboarding evidence and the strongest competing response to the competitor’s pricing pressure. I currently favor simplifying onboarding because completion and activation are both deteriorating, while it can improve time-to-value without immediately reducing price realization. Run a guarded test with qualified-revenue, retention, and customer-quality guardrails so an activation lift does not mask downstream value loss.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding, since the verified source shows +13% completion, 2.1 fewer days to value, and +3% 30-day retention—directly addressing both current completion and activation declines. Do not pursue targeted promotional pricing: despite +18% qualified revenue initially, the 40% discount produced a 12% retention decline and failed the sustainable-growth objective. Evaluate activation alongside qualified revenue, renewal/retention, and account quality to prevent optimizing only for early conversion.
